questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: What does an edge in a pipeline DAG represent?
options: A required dependency: the downstream task may run only once the upstream succeeds
A data channel through which the upstream task streams its rows downstream
A retry relationship, so a failed task falls back to the task it points at
A scheduling hint the scheduler may reorder when workers are contended

questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: Why must retried tasks be idempotent?
options: Because a retry runs on a different worker with a different logical date
Because repeating an attempt must not duplicate or corrupt the logical output
Because the scheduler cannot tell a retry apart from a scheduled run
Because retries execute concurrently with the attempt that is still running

questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: What is the benefit of removing an unnecessary dependency edge?
options: Retries become cheaper because fewer descendants are marked stale
The scheduler can pack more runs into the same concurrency budget
Independent tasks run in parallel, shortening the critical path
Failed tasks stop blocking descendants that never used their output

questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: How should a backfill choose its code version?
options: Track whatever is currently deployed so history matches production logic
Use the version that was live when each historical interval originally ran
Re-resolve dependencies per partition so each uses its newest compatible build
Pin one deliberately selected immutable version for the whole range

questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: A task writes half a partition and fails. What is the safest retry pattern?
options: Stage a complete deterministic replacement, validate it, then commit atomically
Resume from the last row written so the completed work is not recomputed
Delete the partition, then append the retry's output directly into the target
Mark the partial output complete and let the next scheduled run correct it

questions.topic: DAGs: Dependencies, Retries, and Backfill Runs
questions.question: Why can enabling catchup unexpectedly overload a platform?
options: It reruns every task in the DAG rather than only the ones that failed
It may schedule a separate run for every interval missed since the start date
It ignores the maximum-active-runs limit while it is clearing the backlog
It raises each historical run's priority above the current production runs

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: Which workload most strongly fits Airflow or Composer?
options: A single long-running job that reports its own progress externally
An event-driven sequence triggered by individual user requests
Recurring data DAGs with data intervals, backfills and many dependencies
A set of independent scripts with no ordering requirements between them

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: Which workload most strongly fits a cloud workflows service?
options: Distributed aggregation of terabytes held inside the workflow's own state
Historical partition scheduling with catchup across several years
Continuous event-time windowing over an unbounded input stream
A request-driven sequence of managed API calls, branches and waits

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: Why use a deferrable sensor instead of a blocking sensor?
options: It releases its worker slot while waiting instead of occupying one
It shortens the wait by polling the upstream dependency more often
It fails fast when the awaited condition cannot be satisfied at all
It lets the awaited task signal completion rather than being polled

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: Where should large transformation logic normally live?
options: Inside operator definitions, so the DAG file is the single source of truth
In versioned, testable jobs or SQL models that the orchestrator launches
In the workflow state payload, so each step receives the data it needs
In shared plugin modules the scheduler imports when it parses the DAG

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: Two nested orchestrators both retry a failing API call five times. What is the risk?
options: The inner retries are cancelled when the outer orchestrator's timeout fires
The call is retried five times in total, but the failure is reported twice
Attempts multiply to twenty-five and can overwhelm the dependency
The outer orchestrator marks the step successful once the inner one exits

questions.topic: Airflow/Composer vs Workflows: Choosing an Orchestrator
questions.question: What should determine orchestrator choice most directly?
options: The language the team's transformation code is already written in
Whether the platform team can run a scheduler and metadata database
The volume of data each individual task is expected to process
Control-flow shape, recovery, backfill, quota and ownership requirements

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: What is a validation gate?
options: A condition staged data must pass before it becomes visible to consumers
A monitor that alerts when published data drifts from its historical baseline
A schema check the warehouse applies automatically as rows are written
A review step where an owner approves the run before the task is marked done

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: Which test is normally a structural invariant?
options: Daily revenue must stay within twenty percent of the trailing average
Primary keys in the published table must be unique
The freshest partition must be no more than one hour behind the source
Null rates per column must match the distribution seen last month

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: Why is a nonzero row-count check often too weak?
options: It passes even when every row fails the table's uniqueness constraint
It cannot be evaluated until the whole partition has finished loading
A ninety-nine percent data loss still leaves a nonzero row count
It fails on normal daily growth, so teams disable it within a week

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: How should a crash in a blocking validation test be treated?
options: As a pass, since no expectation actually reported a violation
As informational, with the run continuing and the crash logged for review
As a retryable fault, publishing once a later attempt completes cleanly
As a failed gate that blocks publication until it is resolved

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: Which injected fault best proves a uniqueness gate blocks publication?
options: A staged batch containing a deliberately duplicated primary key
A staged batch whose row count is far below the historical baseline
A staged batch with a column renamed so the schema no longer matches
A staged batch delivered hours later than its freshness SLA permits

questions.topic: Validation Gates and Data Quality Testing
questions.question: Why must sampled quality tests state detection power?
options: Because sampling cost scales with the number of partitions examined
Because a sample limits what can be concluded about rare defects
Because samples must be drawn uniformly to satisfy audit requirements
Because the sample size determines how long the gate holds publication

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: What should a pipeline run record for reproducibility?
options: The owning team, the schedule interval and the alert channel it notifies
The wall-clock duration and peak resource usage of every task attempt
Exact code, configuration, artifact and input snapshot versions
The upstream partitions it read and the downstream tables it wrote

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: What is the recommended relationship between deployment and historical backfill?
options: Ship them together so code and history can never disagree with each other
Backfill first, so the new code only ever reads data in its new shape
Backfill automatically after each deploy, bounded by a concurrency limit
Deploy compatible code first, validate a canary, then run an explicit backfill

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: Why should promotion reuse the same immutable artifact across environments?
options: Rebuilding between environments can introduce supply-chain and dependency drift
Rebuilding invalidates the approval, so the change must be reviewed again
Environment endpoints have to be compiled into the image before promotion
Artifact digests are recomputed at runtime and stop matching the manifest

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: Why does reverting DAG code not automatically undo bad data?
options: The revert only takes effect once the scheduler reparses the DAG file
Committed partitions persist independently of whichever code is deployed
Rollback restores the code but replays the runs that produced the data
The metadata database keeps the old run history and reports it as current

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: What is the safest sequence for a field replacement?
options: Deploy dual-writing producers, drop the old field, then migrate the readers
Backfill the new field first so readers never observe a partially filled column
Deploy tolerant readers and dual writers, backfill and validate, migrate, then contract
Introduce the new field under the old name so no consumer has to be changed

questions.topic: CI/CD for Pipelines: Versioned DAGs and Deploy-Then-Backfill
questions.question: What should a backfill manifest contain?
options: The owning team and the approval record for the release being backfilled
The partitions that completed, so a rerun can skip the finished work
The resource limits applied, so the cost can be attributed afterwards
Explicit partition scope, per-partition status, version and recovery information
